text: Your credit journey Understand the complete pathway before exploring each credit Each credit develops a distinct area of strategic capability and produces practical evidence that can be applied in the workplace. 6 Strategic Pathway credits Important: the word credit explains the College pathway structure. These are not regulated or transferable higher-education academic credits. 1–2 PMP Strategic Project Leadership Leadership, governance, delivery confidence, business outcomes and strategic decision-making. 8 months 3 AI in Project Controls Governed automation, data models, dashboards, human approval and responsible AI use. 4 months 4 PRINCE2 Programme Management Programme vision, governance, dependencies, assurance, outcomes and benefits. 4 months 5 PRINCE2 Portfolio Management Prioritisation, investment, portfolio balance, capacity and strategic alignment. 4 months 6 PMI-PMOCP Preparation and PMO Leadership PMO mandate, operating model, services, maturity, leadership and value delivery. 4 months Need help selecting the right route? The admissions team can review your role, prior learning, employer support and evidence opportunities before the training plan is agreed. Book an information session

From evidence to action Strategic controls should improve the quality of real decisions The pathway connects credible project data with programme governance, portfolio investment and PMO leadership. Learners are expected to show how their analysis supports a decision, reveals uncertainty and creates organisational value. Reliable evidence Traceable information across scope, schedule, cost, risk and benefits. Clear recommendations Decisions supported by assumptions, options and visible uncertainty. Practical value Outputs designed for projects, programmes, portfolios and PMO environments.

Who should apply? For professionals who use controls evidence to influence decisions The pathway is designed for experienced professionals with access to suitable strategic activity, credible workplace evidence and employer support. Project-controls leadership Professionals responsible for integrated controls, performance, forecasting and delivery confidence. Heads of project controls Project controls managers Senior planning and cost professionals Risk and assurance practitioners Programme and portfolio roles Professionals connecting project evidence with programme outcomes, investment priorities and organisational capacity. Programme-controls professionals Portfolio governance specialists Transformation professionals Benefits and investment roles PMO and delivery leadership Professionals shaping governance, assurance, decision support and delivery capability. Heads of PMO PMO managers Strategic delivery leaders Governance and assurance professionals Role suitability: a senior job title is not enough. The role must provide a substantial link to ST0845, suitable workplace activity and enough scope to develop significant new occupational competence.

Eligibility criteria Could this apprenticeship pathway be right for you? College of Project Controls completes a role, suitability, prior-learning and funding review before enrolment. Use this guide and quick check as an initial indication only. 1 UK resident for the past 3 years You must have lived in the UK for the past 3 years. 2 Must not require sponsorship to work You must hold a British Passport, Indefinite Leave to Remain, or a Tier 2 visa with at least three years of UK residency. 3 Not enrolled in other government-funded training You must not be enrolled in other government-funded training at the time of this programme. 4 Self-employed individuals are not eligible Self-employed individuals are not eligible for DfE funding. 5 Paid employment in England You must be in paid employment in England, normally 30+ hours per week, with a minimum of 16 hours. 6 Employer based in England Your employer must be based in England and registered with the Apprenticeship Service. 7 Spend at least 50% of working hours in England You must spend at least 50% of your working hours within England. This is an indication only and does not guarantee eligibility, funding or enrolment. Final suitability is confirmed after the College's full role, prior-learning, employer-support and funding review. Account Levy account funds Levy account funds can be used where sufficient funds are available. 75% Levy shortfall Government contribution for levy employers with insufficient funds; employer contribution 25%. 100% Eligible non-levy starts aged 16–24 Government contribution for eligible non-levy employers where the apprentice meets the applicable age requirements. 95% Eligible non-levy starts aged 25+ Government contribution for eligible non-levy employers; employer contribution 5%. £27,000 Maximum funding band The final price must reflect prior learning and be agreed with the employer. No apprentice contribution to eligible costs Employers pay costs above the funding-band maximum Exam costs are included only when confirmed in writing Discuss funding Funding rules, standards, certification names and included benefits may change. The signed apprenticeship agreement, training plan, employer contract and learner offer take precedence over promotional material.

How you study A practical learning cycle built around workplace application Learning is developed through live teaching, guided study, coaching, evidence production and structured review. 1 Learn Explore frameworks, tools, worked examples and professional practice. 2 Apply Use the learning in a real or approved workplace situation. 3 Evidence Capture outputs, decisions, feedback, judgement and impact. 4 Review Discuss progress, KSB coverage and evidence with the coach. 5 Improve Refine the output and agree the next practical development action. Live teaching Interactive online sessions, technical discussion, strategic cases and worked examples. Skills coaching Regular support for evidence, reflection, progress and assessment readiness. Workplace application Real projects, employer feedback and practical outputs connected to the occupational standard.

External certifications remain independently awarded.
